decisionMemo.businessProblem: A regional regulated electric utility with stable ~$3B revenue and stable EBITDA is steadily under-earning its allowed return. Its earned ROE has fallen from 9.5% (FY2023) to 8.2% (FY2025), now ~160 bps below the 9.8% ROE authorized in its last rate case. The structural driver is a mismatch between the regulated pricing mechanism and the capital cost trajectory: approved revenue is permitted to grow only ~2.4%/yr (within a 2-3% band), while the company must deploy $1,100M/yr of largely mandated capital (grid hardening, reliability, decarbonization) against only ~$650M of depreciation (capex/depreciation 1.69x), and the unit cost of that capital is inflating ~9%/yr. Because rates are set via a historical test year and reset only every ~3 years, current rates reflect a cost picture ~24 months stale, so the utility chronically under-recovers the cost of capital it has already put into service (regulatory lag / under-recovery). O&M is run lean and is roughly flat, so the gap is not operating-cost bloat or a demand problem. The core question: is the realized-return erosion an operations/cost issue, a demand issue, or a structural mismatch between the regulator-approved rate mechanism and the inflating capital plan — and what should management do before the next rate-case filing window (~120-180 days) to stop locking in another multi-year cycle of under-earning?
